title: Beyond the Anxious Child: Mapping Provider Stress, Confidence and Empathy in Paediatric Dentistry—A Scoping Review
content: Background/Objectives: Provider affect, preparedness and empathy may influence behaviour guidance in paediatric dentistry, but their measurement alongside observed clinical behaviour and child-level responses has not been systematically mapped. Methods: A protocol-registered scoping review followed JBI guidance and PRISMA-ScR. Nine databases and complementary sources were searched, and eligible primary reports were charted by study family. Measurement domains were coded as clinician-reported, physiological, independently observed, child-level or caregiver-level. Results: Thirty-three reports representing 32 study families met the criteria. Principal constructs were stress/anxiety/coping (n = 19), confidence/preparedness (n = 9) and empathy (n = 4). Twenty-five families (78.1%) used provider self-report alone; five included child-level measures or treatment-related endpoints, and one independently assessed clinician behaviour. No study family co-measured a provider construct, observed clinical behaviour and a child-level measure. Conclusions: Existing studies describe clinician experiences much more frequently than the actions taken during treatment. Integrating provider-state measures, observed chairside conduct and child responses within the same encounters is the clearest next step for understanding behaviour guidance and evaluating educational transfer.
